findings.detail: `_polygon_current_response` duplicates a capability the repository already owns: `nova/biot/polygonanalytic.py:1933 polygon_analytic_greens` returns psi, B_R and B_Z per unit azimuthal current density for a polygon section in closed form, and this function returns the same quantity through the traced quadrature kernel `_traced_psi_gradient` instead of extending that owner. The duplicate is validated against the owner (tests/test_magnetisation.py:1110 pins agreement to 2e-8 on a 10 mm triangle, and the fragment records 1.74e-11 at 128 nodes) and is kept for a measured cost reason -- the closed owner did not finish a shell assembly in about two hours on the P100 -- so it is recorded, not corrected; a later node should fold the two routes into one owner behind a route flag, as the sheet module already does.

The module's declared public surface is `__all__` at line 1849, and none of `linear_magnetisation_geometry` (1876), `linear_galerkin_cell_interaction` (2113) or `linear_cell_interaction` (2177) is listed in it, although `nova/biot/magnetisation.py:28-30` imports all three as the module's extension. A reader who takes `__all__` as the module's API cannot see the capability this node landed.

The column headed `gram` symmetry defect reports `galerkin_spectrum(...)["volume_symmetry"]`, which `nova/biot/magnetisation.py:277-282` computes as the asymmetry of `metric @ gram / mu0`, the volume-weighted energy, not of the Gram matrix H itself. The values (9.18e-17, 1.21e-16) reproduce exactly from the run's own logs, so the measurement is sound; the label names a different matrix than the one measured.

The node's declared evidence fence asks for the mu_r 1000 shell at uniform 40, 20 and 10 mm with the order between successive halvings; the 10 mm arm is `completed: false` in /work/projects/imas_gpu/sophelio/evidence/iron-core-magnetisation/linear-magnetisation/linear-0.01.json (assembly 8906.079 s, Newton update RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED), so the measure is two of three spacings and one halving order, not two. The gap is stated in the fragment rather than concealed, and the coordinator's status-repair record for this run (review path .../status-repair.json) records a lead ruling of 2026-11-14 that lands the two completed rows and folds the 10 mm row and the per-cell assembly cost to a new section-5 node; folded there, which is why this finding does not hold the node.

The `after_suite` arm names revision b3b57437ec271a0172a7dc9aaab6e2351fedaf69 while the reviewed head is be8a601672fc. Nine commits lie between them, and I verified by diff that no product source or test file changes across the gap: `nova/biot/magnetisation.py` differs only in the ValueError message for an invalid seed shape, and `nova/biot/tiledassembly.py` does not differ at all, so the 59-pass arm does cover the delivered source. The record still names a revision that is not the one being promoted, and the fragment states this explicitly.

verdicts.text: The node's goal is to build piecewise-linear magnetisation on the Galerkin iron route and measure it on the mu_r 1000 closed shell; nova/biot/magnetisation.py:582 solve_magnetisation gains `basis="linear"` with six unknowns per cell, nova/biot/tiledassembly.py:1876 linear_magnetisation_geometry and nova/biot/tiledassembly.py:2113 linear_galerkin_cell_interaction build the operator, and the shell is measured at 40 and 20 mm but not the third spacing the evidence fence names.

The declared done-when has three clauses: a fast spectrum/negative-control/bit-identity clause is asserted by tests/test_magnetisation.py:1040 with a red control at validated-fast/negative-control.log (2 failed, EXIT=1, maxima 1.9204 and 2.1229 against the 1.0 bound), and the constant basis is pinned by the base arm's 53 passed; the receipt clause is met for 40 and 20 mm only, with linear-0.01.json recording completed:false; the fragment-and-figure clause is answered in docs/evidence/fragments/iron-core-magnetisation/icm-linear-magnetisation.html and the inspected SVG.

Declared paths are nova/biot/magnetisation.py, nova/biot/tiledassembly.py, tests/test_magnetisation.py, scripts/iron_linear_magnetisation, scripts/iron_graded_refinement/gate.sh, the evidence fragment and its figures directory; all 16 files of the diff (git diff --stat 60d418bb..be8a60167) sit inside those paths, and no path outside them is touched.
